text: Applying Gradual Magnitude Pruning (GMP) and Sparse Evolutionary Training (SET) consistently modifies three correlative indicators of plasticity in multi-task agents trained on the three MiniGrid benchmarks MT3, MT5, and MT7.

Across the two MTRL architectures, shared-backbone MTPPO and Mixture-of-Experts (MoE), and the three MiniGrid benchmarks, MT3, MT5, and MT7, agents trained with GMP (final target sparsity 95% in main experiments) or SET (fixed sparsity 95% with ERK initialization and evolution parameter ε) achieve higher normalized interquantile mean (IQM) aggregate returns than their dense counterparts.
GMP at 99% sparsity can produce rank collapse in Mixture of Orthogonal Experts (MOORE).
